isolation_policy: bubblewrap mount namespace: only the workspace, the policy-accepted read allowlist and the opencode runtime exist; the repository, the other arms' results, the earlier sessions and the global opencode configuration (its MCP servers and plugins) are not mounted; plus the opencode v2 permission object (bash denied, edit and write denied, read and external_directory deny-by-default with the explicit allowlist)
limitations: The mount namespace is the filesystem guarantee; the model provider is reachable over the shared network, so a model that was shown a file can still send it away.
sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT:
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: SUCC-GEO-CBTAB
TITLE: Behaviour-weighted geodesic triplet margin that moves the shared RQ codebook table so successor items' hierarchical code prefixes are Poincare-close
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built for reconstruction, not for transitions. Two items a user actually moves between often land on unrelated prefixes, so the generative recommender must memorise the transition instead of reading it off the code tree. The fix cannot be "add a graph loss", because a flat Euclidean graph loss just pulls code vectors together and collapses the codebook; the natural geometry for a tree-shaped prefix code with an exponentially growing frontier is negative curvature.
NOVELTY: Prior rounds put curvature on the assignment (Sinkhorn / voronoi / curvature cells), on transported tangent frames (fork angle, shell, cone), or on anchored charts. This one leaves the assignment, the encoder and the Sinkhorn machinery completely untouched and puts the curved operation on the CODEBOOK UPDATE: a curvature-measured geodesic triplet margin over prefix-truncated code sums, with the margin violation weighted by a row-normalised transition strength. It is a code-table geometry, not an assignment geometry, not a transport, not a chart, and not an auxiliary hyperbolic head on the encoder.
CHANGE: After each epoch we snapshot every training item's L code indices (free: they come from the forward passes already run). Each step we sample training-only transitions, form prefix code sums at levels 1, 2 and L, map them by exp_0^kappa into a Poincare ball of fixed measured curvature -kappa, and apply a softplus triplet margin in which the positive/negative geodesic gap is multiplied by the transition weight; gradient flows into the codebooks only.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'see SPEC EQUATIONS.'}
COST: No extra forward passes and no extra encoder compute. Per step at the frozen scale: 1024 sampled transitions x 3 prefix depths x 2 distances (positive and negative) = 6144 Poincare distance evaluations at dimension d (64-128), about 0.5 MFLOP, plus 3 gather-sums over 3 tables per endpoint, i.e. under 0.5 percent of one optimizer step. Cache refresh is O(24556 x 3) integer writes once per epoch (72000 steps over 3000 epochs; 24 steps per epoch). Memory: 24556 x 3 int32 = 295 KB. Expected wall-clock delta on four cards: under 1 percent.
HYPOTHESIS: If the successor table carries usable structure at the granularity of code prefixes, then a behaviour-weighted geodesic margin on the codebook should raise the fraction of transitions whose successor shares the anchor's level-1 and level-2 code above the reconstruction-only baseline, and that gain should carry into Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 without any change to the Stage 3 protocol. Observed through: successor-prefix hit rate per level, codebook usage entropy, mean geodesic distance of true successor pairs versus random pairs, and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10 on the single run.
RISKS: ['(a) Codebook-only gradient may be too slow to relocate codes within 3000 epochs, leaving SIDs close to baseline. (b) Negative sampling noise can pull unrelated items together when the table is sparse (cold items with one transition). (c) The margin can be satisfied by driving two items to identical codes, which would help the objective but destroy SID uniqueness and hurt generation; a duplicate-count diagnostic covers this. (d) If code sums sit very near the origin the derived curvature is too flat and Poincare distance degenerates toward Euclidean, so the coupling becomes numerically inert.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS
TITLE: Behaviour-mass weighted Karcher (Poincare) codebook estimation for the RQ-VAE semantic-ID quantizer.
MOTIVATION: Every existing curved-SID mechanism moves the *assignment* (curved cost, Sinkhorn, cones, shells) or the *residual* (transport), while leaving the estimator untouched: a code vector is still a Euclidean centroid of its assigned points. Consequence: a code is pulled by the raw item cloud, so behaviourally central items (the ones that actually determine what follows what) get exactly as much say in the code position as dead-tail items that merely happen to land in the same cell. Behaviourally coherent prefixes therefore stay diluted, and the generative recommender is asked to predict tokens whose geometry was never shaped by transitions.
NOVELTY: The curved operation is placed on the code-vector *estimator*, not on the cost. Each code is computed as a behaviour-weighted Frechet (Karcher) mean in the Poincare ball, so (i) the behaviour signal changes which assigned points dominate the code, and (ii) curvature changes how those dominant points pull (hyperbolic log maps grow like log((1+r)/(1-r)), and the Karcher mean contracts toward the ball centre relative to the Euclidean mean). No previous arm in this programme estimated codes geodesically; nothing here reuses a Sinkhorn cost, a tangent-space fork transport, a radial shell/volume scalar, a margin/cone, or a per-node curvature field.
CHANGE: Replace the quantizer's Euclidean code-vector update (EMA centroid or gradient step) by a single Riemannian Karcher step in the Poincare ball, with each assigned residual point reweighted by a popularity-adjusted transition centrality of its item. Assignment code path, encoder, decoder, loss and Stage 3 are untouched.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Chart the latent: p = z/(||z||+tau), tau = median ||z|| measured once over the frozen 24,556 Stage-2 items; curvature c = 1 (unit negative curvature, ball radius 1). For each level l and each code k with assigned points p_i and item weights w_i: g_k = sum_i w_i * log_{m_k}(p_i) / sum_i w_i ; m_k <- exp_{m_k}( eta_k * g_k ) ; eta_k = 1/(1+N_k) with N_k the raw (unweighted) assignment count. Behaviour enters only through w_i; geometry enters only through log/exp and the metric factor lambda. w_i = 1 + log1p( mu_tilde(x_i) ) where mu_tilde is the transition-centrality normalized to mean 1 and clipped at its data 99th percentile.'}
COST: Stage 2 is 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72,000 steps at 24,556 items (~1023 items/step). Per step the update touches 3 levels x ~1023 points x d=64: about 2e5 elementwise ops (two Mobius additions, one artanh, one tanh per point-level), fully vectorised, well under 1 ms on one GPU against a typical 50-150 ms encoder step, i.e. an estimated +1 to +3 percent Stage-2 wall clock, roughly +2 to +5 minutes over the whole 72,000 steps. One-off preprocessing: counting training transitions (a few million pairs) plus one forward pass over 24,556 items to measure tau: about 1 to 2 minutes. Stage 3 cost is exactly zero (it consumes integer SIDs). No extra epochs, no extra forward or backward passes, no extra parameters.
HYPOTHESIS: If within-cell transition mass is strongly heterogeneous (heavy-tailed popularity gives mu_tilde coefficients of variation well above 1 inside most cells) and the hyperbolic Karcher mean materially relocates codes, then hub-adjacent items get finer effective resolution and SID prefixes become more behaviourally predictable, lifting Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single coupled run. It is worth keeping if that run exceeds 0.065 AND the logged diagnostics confirm the mechanism actually fired (weight dispersion and code displacement are non-trivial); it is not worth keeping if recall does not move even though the diagnostics show the coupling was active, or if recall moves while the diagnostics show the weights were nearly uniform.
RISKS: ['The 99th-percentile clip could still let a handful of hub items dominate a cell, collapsing several codes toward the same region and creating prefix collisions. The hyperbolic mean contracts codes toward the ball centre, which may crowd many codes into the inner region and destroy the radial spread the frozen quantizer relied on. Long-tail data may make mu_tilde nearly uniform for the bulk of items so the mechanism barely fires. If the frozen quantizer already assigns under a hyperbolic metric, the interaction with a curved estimator may be redundant or unstable. A single run cannot separate a real gain from seed noise, so a marginal improvement (e.g. 0.0655) is not evidence.']
END IDEA

IDEA: MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-gated mixed-curvature product codebook: each item is quantized under a Poincare factor or a spherical factor according to how tree-like its training transition neighbourhood is
MOTIVATION: A single negative-curvature SID model assumes the item transition graph is a tree: one radial "is-a / sequel-of" depth plus an angular sector. Real consumption is a mixture. Sequel and attribute chains are tree-like, but repeat consumption, substitutes and mutually linked co-consumption form short cycles, and a Poincare ball can only represent a cycle by spending radial depth, which pushes cyclically consumed items onto the boundary where the metric is numerically hostile and where their prefixes collide with unrelated leaf items. The result is SIDs whose first tokens mix two incompatible kinds of neighbourhood, so the Stage 3 generator sees a prefix whose next-token distribution is a superposition of a hierarchy move and a lateral move, which is exactly the regime where prefix prediction degrades. The proposal gives each item its own curvature mixture, measured from its own training transitions, so the partition can be hierarchical where the behaviour is hierarchical and lateral where the behaviour is lateral.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here either weight/diffuse the assignment mass (cocond-markov-poincare-ot), place a hierarchy in one negative-curvature latent (BRANCHCURV-SID, KAPPA_BRANCH, GEO-SHELL-RQ, CURVCELL-SID, SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ), transport successor directions in the tangent space (fork-angle-transport, fork-angular-barycenter, SUCC-TAN-RQ), use geodesic charts/anchors, or use a Lorentz cone. None uses a positive-curvature factor at all, none uses a product of two manifolds of opposite curvature, and none makes a measured per-item behaviour statistic choose the metric an item is quantized under. Here the behaviour statistic is not a weight on a distance and not a target shift: it is the mixing coordinate between a hyperbolic and a spherical metric, so removing it collapses to an unweighted product metric and removing curvature collapses to a plain weighted Euclidean quantizer.
CHANGE: The RQ-VAE codebook stops being a set of vectors in one Euclidean (or one Poincare) space and becomes a set of product-manifold points (a ball point, a sphere point) per level, with each item's assignment distance being a behaviour-weighted combination of the Poincare distance in the first factor and the spherical geodesic distance in the second. The same behaviour weight also enters the Frechet/Karcher codebook estimator, so the per-item tree-likeness statistic changes both which code an item gets and where the code sits.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Precompute once on the Stage-2 training sequences only. Add a directed edge u_t -> u_{t+1} for every consecutive pair inside every training sequence. For item i let N_i be its out-neighbour set, k_i = |N_i|, and c_i the number of ordered pairs (a,b) in N_i x N_i with a != b and an edge a -> b; C_i = c_i / (k_i (k_i - 1)) if k_i >= 2 else 0 (this is the directed local clustering coefficient, i.e. how much i's successors feed each other = how cyclic/lateral rather than tree-like i's consumption role is). Define the tree-likeness weight g_i = clip(1 - C_i, 0.1, 0.9); if k_i < 5 set g_i = 0.5. The 0.1/0.9 clip and the 0.5 low-degree prior are fixed documented defaults, not tuned. At every RQ level l in 1..3 the encoder output z in R^d is split into z_H in R^{d_H} (d_H = ceil(d/2)) and z_S in R^{d_S} (d_S = d - d_H); the running reconstruction zhat starts at 0; p = exp0^{k_H}(zhat_H) is a Poincare ball point and q = R_S * zhat_S/||zhat_S|| is a point on the sphere of radius R_S = 1/sqrt(k_S); codebook entry k of level l is (A_lk, B_lk) with ||B_lk|| = R_S; the assignment uses D_ik = sqrt( g_i * dtil_H(p, A_lk)^2 + (1 - g_i) * dtil_S(q, B_lk)^2 ) with both factor distances normalised by their own derived maximum so that g_i is a genuine mixing coordinate; the straight-through code is the baseline's, with the baseline temperature reused unchanged; after choosing k*, zhat_H += log0^{k_H}(A_lk*) and zhat_S += B_lk* - q_base where q_base is the unnormalised zhat_S, i.e. the spherical factor advances by the chord to the chosen sphere point while the hyperbolic factor advances by the tangent image of the chosen ball point; the decoder and the commitment loss see zhat exactly as in the baseline. k_H and k_S are trainable via k = softplus(k_raw) + 1e-3, initialised at k_H = k_S = 1.0 (unit curvature, documented default). Codebook entries are updated by one Karcher/Frechet step per level with the same g_i: A_lk <- exp0^{k_H}( sum_i s_ik g_i log0^{k_H}(p_i) / sum_i s_ik g_i ), B_lk <- R_S * normalise( sum_i s_ik (1 - g_i) q_i ), where s_ik is the soft assignment mass of item i to code k."}
COST: No new parameters of consequence (3 x 256 x d product codebook points, plus the 24556-vector g). One-time graph pass over the training transitions, O(E) with E = number of consecutive pairs (order 10^6), a few seconds and a 24556-element output. Per step at the frozen scale only 24556/24 ~= 1023 items are quantized against 3 x 256 codes, i.e. ~7.9e5 product distances per step, each costing one arcosh plus one arccos over d-dimension inner products; this is roughly 3-5x the baseline Euclidean squared-distance kernel, which is itself a sub-millisecond, launch-bound slice of a Stage-2 step, so the expected per-step overhead is well under 1% of a Stage-2 step and under 2-3% of total wall clock over 3000 x 24 = 72000 steps. Memory overhead is negligible. No sweep, no extra seed, no extra arm: one training run.
HYPOTHESIS: If per-item behaviour tree-likeness is a real signal, then items whose training transitions are strongly cyclic are currently being forced into a hierarchy their behaviour does not have, and giving them a spherical fibre should (a) reduce prefix collisions between behaviourally distinct items in the tail, (b) lower the Stage 3 generator's cross-entropy on tokens 2 and 3 relative to token 1, and (c) raise Stage 3 test recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run. It is worth keeping if and only if the run both beats 0.065 and shows level-1 token usage that tracks the behaviour communities rather than collapsing onto a few radial shells.
RISKS: ['C_i is noisy for low-degree items, which are the majority of the long tail, so g_i may be near its 0.5 prior for most items and the mechanism may act only on the head; the spherical factor may simply add an uninformative rotational degree of freedom that the decoder ignores, in which case tokens 2-3 get noisier; the two curvature scales interact with the straight-through temperature, and although the temperature is inherited unchanged, a badly conditioned initial ball radius can make the arcosh term dominate early; and a gain could come from the extra geometry with zero contribution from behaviour, which the diagnostics must expose rather than the run hiding.']
END IDEA

IDEA: poincare-frechet-successor-codebook
TITLE: Curved successor-weighted Fréchet codebook updates for the RQ-VAE residual quantizer
MOTIVATION: The SID vocabulary is not the encoder, it is the codebook. Standard RQ-VAE trains every item latent with equal weight, so codebook slots are spent on popular but behaviourally interchangeable items, and the first prefixes do not separate items that actually follow one another. Directed successor flow is the cheapest evidence of which items deserve to share a slot or a prefix, yet it currently never reaches the estimator that produces the codebook.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds placed behaviour and curvature in the assignment step (Poincaré-cost Sinkhorn, successor-fork angles, cones, shells, geodesic charts, target transport). This proposal leaves the assignment cost untouched and instead changes the estimator that produces the codebook itself: every slot is moved by a weighted Riemannian Fréchet step in the Poincaré ball, so the SID vocabulary is learned, not merely assigned, under a curved behaviour-weighted objective. No OT, no fork angle, no cone, no shell, no per-prefix curvature.
CHANGE: Replace the RQ-VAE codebook EMA/gradient update with a per-slot Poincaré Fréchet step whose per-item weights are the training-only, popularity-adjusted successor attraction of each item, and use the same weights inside the commitment term so the encoder and the codebook are pulled by one weighted geodesic objective.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Fixed curvature kappa = -1 (documented default, never swept). Encoder emits e_i in R^d; map to the ball as z_i = exp_0^kappa( tanh(||e_i||) * e_i / (||e_i|| * sqrt(|kappa|)) ), which lands strictly inside the ball. For each residual level l = 1..3 with codebook C_l = {c_{l,k}} subset B^d: assignment a_l(i) = argmin_k d_kappa(z_i, c_{l,k}); commitment L_l = sum_i w_i * d_kappa(z_i, sg[c_{l,a(i)}])^2 plus reconstruction as in the baseline. Codebook update, per step, per level, for each slot k with S_k = {i : a(i) = k}: m_k = sum_{i in S_k} w_i * log^kappa_{c_k}(z_i) / sum_{i in S_k} w_i ; c_k <- exp^kappa_{c_k}( eta * m_k ), eta = 1. Residual r_i = log^kappa_{c_{l,a(i)}}(z_i) is fed to level l+1 as usual. Behaviour weights, training split only: count directed adjacent pairs (u -> v) inside train sessions, indeg_v = sum_u n_uv, n_v = train interaction count of v, w_v = (indeg_v + 1) / (n_v + 2) (Beta(1,1) posterior mean, in (0,1]), clip to [0.25, 4], then per-batch normalise w_hat_i = w_i / mean_batch(w). The codebook update is detached (sg), so it is an estimator, not a gradient path; the encoder still gets gradients through d_kappa and the commitment term. Self-transitions are removed before counting.'}
COST: One-off transition counting over train sessions, O(number of train transitions), under 2 s. Per step at the frozen scale (B = 1024, L = 3, d = 64): one extra Poincaré exp/log pair over B*L*d ≈ 2e5 floats plus one scatter-add, about 3–6% of step time, and a weighted commitment that is negligible. Across 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps this is roughly +5–10% Stage2 wall clock, with no extra forward or backward pass and only a detached tangent buffer of B*L*d floats in memory.
HYPOTHESIS: If successor-attracting items share codebook slots, then level-1 and level-2 prefixes become behaviourally predictive and the Stage3 generator's prefix-constrained decoding proposes better candidates, lifting test Recall@10 above 0.065. It is worth keeping only if the weighted Fréchet displacement concentrates on high-w slots, prefix→successor conditional entropy on train sequences falls relative to the unweighted codebook, and the Recall@10 gain is concentrated on high-w and high-predecessor-concentration items rather than spread uniformly.
RISKS: ["The Fréchet step can be unstable or collapse several slots onto one high-w region; the weights can degrade into a popularity proxy if indeg and n_v are too collinear; codebook drift can hurt reconstruction and therefore the generator's conditioning; a single eta = 1 step is only a first-order approximation of the weighted Fréchet mean and may lag; the gain may be smaller than single-run seed noise."]
END IDEA
